methods.name: WeightIt logistic (glm) propensity weights: ATE, ATT, ATC, stabilised ATE
Entropy balancing (WeightIt ebal and the exact convex dual): ATE, ATT, ATC; ESS per group
methods.reference: WeightIt::weightit(method = 'ebal', estimand); exact dual min log sum exp(lambda'(x_i - t)) by Newton to |grad| < 1e-14
methods.tolerance: exact dual 1e-8 relative (Tol::coef(300)); ESS 1e-6 (Tol::stat); WeightIt optim values 1e-4 relative (cross-check)

methods.name: Energy balancing (Huling & Mak 2022): ATT, ATC, improved ATE
methods.reference: energy-distance QP on standardised covariates (WeightIt weightit2energy's P and q at lambda = 0, min.w = 0) solved with quadprog::solve.QP; WeightIt 'energy' needs osqp (not installed)
methods.tolerance: weights 1e-8 relative + 1e-10 absolute; effects and energy 1e-8 relative (Tol::coef(300)); zero counts exact

methods.name: WeightIt 'stable': stable balancing weights with exact balance (optweight, tols = 0)
methods.reference: Zubizarreta (2015) SBW QP with exact balance, solved with quadprog::solve.QP (optweight not installed)

methods.name: Stable balancing weights: ATT, ATC, ATE; exact and approximate balance
methods.reference: Zubizarreta (2015) QP min sum (w - 1/n)^2, sum w = 1, w >= 0, |sum w x_j - t_j| <= delta sd_j, solved with quadprog::solve.QP
methods.tolerance: weights 1e-8 relative + 1e-12 absolute; objective, means and effect 1e-8 relative (Tol::coef(300)); zero counts exact

methods.name: IPW (Hajek, Horvitz-Thompson, ATT) with EIF, M-estimation and propensity-known standard errors
methods.reference: glm(binomial) propensity; sandwich::vcovHC(type = 'HC0') of lm(y ~ treat, weights); stacked M-estimation sandwich = WeightIt::lm_weightit(vcov = 'asympt')
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 300: effects 1e-8, SEs 1e-6 relative; WeightIt cross-check 1e-6

methods.name: Doubly robust AIPW (ATE, ATT) and regression adjustment
methods.reference: AIPW with OLS outcome models per arm (lm), glm(binomial) propensity; SE sd(psi)/sqrt(n)
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 300: effects 1e-8, SEs and R2 1e-6 relative
